Edit Image 1 to show the same head from behind and on its anatomical left side, a rear-left three-quarter view approximately 135 degrees from front. The near anatomical-left ear is on screen-left. Reproject the entire head, hair and attached ears together.

Image 1 is the character and edit canvas. Preserve identity, expression, hair asymmetry, skin, style and background while reprojecting the whole head and hairstyle into the requested view. Frame the authored hair completely; expand below the head into shoulders or back only when needed to show a meaningful hair endpoint. The source crop does not define the hair endpoint. Keep anatomical attachments fixed on the head; never mirror the image. Supporting images govern only the explicitly assigned features; exclude their material, identity, hairstyle, neck, shoulders, framing and background. They do not override the target camera.

* Image 1 is Youth Tsaeytte's selected FRONT and controls her identity, feature placement, pointed ears, violet eye color, warm skin, art style, lighting, and background. Preserve her full soft cheeks, large natural almond eyes, gentle innocent expression, and established long-hair silhouette.

Keep one continuous, thick black curtain of hair: broad at the crown and across the upper back, gently flared with gentle natural movement, falling behind both shoulders to mid-back, below the shoulder blades, rather than ending or bunching at shoulder height. Keep a few fine face-framing strands without covering the main side panels. Reproject head, ears, and curtain together into each target view. Extend the framing as needed to show the hair's length, including enough shoulders and back below the shoulder blades to establish the endpoint, as framing context only. A crop edge or shortened source hem does not redefine her authored length.

* Rear-left three-quarter view. The broad, gently flared black curtain dominates from crown to a clearly visible, softly rounded U-shaped hemline at mid-back, visibly below the shoulder blades. Show enough upper back beneath the shoulder blades to make that endpoint unmistakable; rear-quarter foreshortening must not raise the hem. At most a narrow cheek edge is visible, with both eyes hidden.

Keep the head upright at eye level. Any visible eyes follow the face direction. Preserve intentional hair occlusion; do not move hair or turn the face to expose hidden features. Keep the complete head and exposed ear tips comfortably inside the frame, with usable head detail and natural head/neck proportions. Frame the head and complete authored hairstyle; expand below the head into shoulder or back context only when needed to show a meaningful hair endpoint. For mid-back hair, include the back below the shoulder blades when that context is needed; do not shorten long hair to fit the source crop. If exceptionally long hair cannot fit while retaining usable head detail, let it continue naturally beyond the lower frame without inventing a shorter hem. Body and clothing are framing context only. Preserve the authored hair length and natural occlusion in the requested view.

# Render Task

Create one finished full-character assembly for Tsaeytte, Youth by joining the supplied head to the supplied body.

# Image Inputs

- **Image 1 — edit_base:** body_reference.
- **Image 2 — subject_reference:** head_image.

# Change Contract

Use Image 1 as the composition base and combine only the explicitly assigned content from the other images.

# Preserve Contract

Preserve all unassigned base-image content. Each other image controls only its stated role.

Image 1 is the supplied body. Image 2 is the supplied head. Use only these two images.

Put the head in Image 2 on the body in Image 1.
- Keep the supplied face, ears, apparent age, expression, and gaze unchanged. Preserve the hairstyle's color, texture, parting, volume and asymmetry.
- Keep the body's proportions, pose, stance, clothing design, framing, background, and orientation unchanged.
- Preserve the head's identity and natural scale relative to the body.
- Join the head and neck naturally, with local blending at the junction. Follow the lower-hair silhouette and endpoint authored in Subject Details while preserving the supplied hairstyle above it.
- Continue the established hairstyle naturally across the necessary shoulders, back and clothing, with correct overlap and perspective. Hair may cover those surfaces without changing underlying body geometry or clothing design. Preserve the supplied hair length outside the authored lower-hair completion. Keep short hairstyles short.
- Preserve the supplied rendering style and detail; do not broadly repaint or reinterpret either source.

# Subject Details

Continue the supplied long black hair behind both shoulders as one broad, thick, gently flared hair curtain. End the lower edge below the shoulder blades at mid-back with a softly rounded U-shaped hemline. Preserve the head reference's part, texture, volume, and asymmetry. Let the lower curtain overlap the back and clothing while preserving the body's shape and clothing design.

* Show the broad curtain over the upper back to below the shoulder blades to mid-back, with its softly rounded U-shaped hemline shortened only by perspective.

Describe visible sides from the camera's view: use screen-left and screen-right for direct front and back views, and near-side and far-side for three-quarter and profile views.
The head, neck, torso, and feet remain aligned in the same back-left three-quarter orientation. Do not introduce independent head rotation at the neck. Do not rotate the head independently of the body. The camera is behind the character, toward screen-left.

THREE-QUARTER ORIENTATION LOCK

The Reference Body and Character Head already use the same back-left three-quarter view. Preserve that shared orientation exactly. The head, neck, and torso remain one aligned unit; do not add independent head yaw, pitch, or roll.

This is a rear-biased view. The back and near side of the head remain dominant. Preserve the Character Head's exact facial-plane direction, feature visibility, and supplied gaze. Do not turn the face toward the viewer or reveal more of the eyes, nose, mouth, cheek, jaw, or expression than is already visible in the Character Head. Any feature hidden or only partly visible in the Character Head must remain similarly hidden or partial. Greater facial visibility is an orientation error.

The supplied sources are already rendered in the same intended style. Preserve that style throughout the image. Allow localized blending, antialiasing, shading adjustment, skin-transition harmonization, edge cleanup and reconstruction at the natural head/neck join. Also allow lower-hair completion only to an endpoint explicitly authored in Subject Details, with natural overlap over shoulders, back and clothing while preserving underlying body geometry and clothing design. Do not broadly repaint or reinterpret the character.

# Constraints

Do not redirect the gaze, change head scale, alter body geometry, mirror the requested view, or redesign the neck, shoulders, hairstyle or body. Limit reconstruction to the natural join and lower-hair completion explicitly authorized in Subject Details; do not expose features naturally hidden by hair.

Produce one character, one view, and one finished image—not a scene, collage, or multi-view sheet.
